theory.overview: Optimization passes transform code to make it faster, smaller, or more energy-efficient. Compilers apply multiple passes: constant folding, dead code elimination, loop optimizations, inlining, and more. Understanding optimizations helps write code that compilers can optimize effectively.

sections.title: Constant Folding
sections.content: Compute constant expressions at compile time. For example, '3 + 4' becomes '7' and 'x * 2 + x * 3' becomes 'x * 5'.

sections.title: Dead Code Elimination
sections.content: Remove code that never executes or whose results are never used. This includes unreachable branches and unused variables.

sections.title: Loop Optimizations
sections.content: Loop unrolling (replicating loop body), loop invariant code motion (moving calculations out of loops), and induction variable optimization.

keyConcepts.name: Inlining
keyConcepts.description: Replace function call with function body

steps.title: Local Optimizations
steps.content: Peephole optimizations examine small instruction windows. Common patterns: 'x = x + 0' eliminated, 'x = x * 1' eliminated, 'x = x * 2' becomes 'x = x << 1'.

steps.title: Global Dataflow Analysis
steps.content: Iterate over control flow graph computing facts about each block: available expressions, live variables, reaching definitions. Use results to enable global optimizations.

steps.title: Loop Analysis
steps.content: Identify loops using dominator analysis. Compute loop invariants, induction variables. Apply loop-specific optimizations.

practiceProblems.title: Constant Folding
practiceProblems.solution: x = 17. Both multiplications and additions of constants are evaluated at compile time.

practiceProblems.title: Invariant Code Motion
practiceProblems.description: for(i=0; i<n; i++) { x = a + b; arr[i] = x; }. What moves out of the loop?
practiceProblems.solution: x = a + b is invariant (doesn't depend on i). Move before the loop: t = a + b; for(...) arr[i] = t;

minigame.title: Code Optimizer
minigame.description: Apply optimization passes to improve code performance

codeExample.code:
# Constant propagation and folding
def optimize_constant_fold(ir):
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        constants = {}  # var -> constant value
        
        for instr in ir:
            # Track constants
            if instr.op == 'const':
                constants[instr.dest] = instr.value
            
            # Constant folding: fold binary ops on constants
            elif instr.op in ('add', 'sub', 'mul', 'div'):
                if instr.left in constants and instr.right in constants:
                    l, r = constants[instr.left], constants[instr.right]
                    result = eval(f'{l} {instr.op[0]} {r}')
                    instr.op = 'const'
                    instr.value = result
                    del instr.left
                    del instr.right
                    constants[instr.dest] = result
                    changed = True
            
            # Constant propagation: replace vars with constants
            elif instr.op in ('add', 'sub', 'mul', 'div'):
                if instr.left in constants:
                    instr.left = constants[instr.left]
                    changed = True
                if instr.right in constants:
                    instr.right = constants[instr.right]
                    changed = True
    
    return ir

# Example: x = 5; y = x + 3; z = y * 2
# Becomes: x = 5; y = 8; z = 16
